title: Water + ethanol + cyclohexane, NRTL, F4's column with 10 mol % cyclohexane in the feed: the entrainer start as the last attempt
purpose: Decision 2026-11-18-04 (the maintainer, 2026-11-18): the entrainer start of proposal 0025 also as the very last attempt. F4's column (20 stages, feed on 5, B = 80 mol/s) with 10 % water and 10 % cyclohexane: the bubble-point starts hold two liquids in the condensate and run, but Newton fails from them and the continuations fail; the entrainer start, tried last, converges.
method_choice: docs/METHOD_SELECTION.md rules 3 and 7: polar, below 10 bar, two liquids: NRTL with the default sets, each fitted to open measured data (ethanol + water fitted-kamihama2012; water + cyclohexane fitted-marche2006-etal, mutual solubilities; ethanol + cyclohexane fitted-reddy2013; src/data/binaries.json), ideal-gas vapour. None was fitted to ternary data.

behaviour: the column converges from the entrainer start, tried after every other attempt failed
the reference's profile, liquids and duties within F1's tolerances
expected.branch: The engine's solution from its entrainer start; the reference (validation/python/reference_mesh_vll.py --entrainer, ChemSep's three-phase stage) solves its own equations from the engine's profile, perturbed.

engine_against_reference.why: Proposal 0015, Engineering basis: flows within 1e-6 relative of the independent MESH solution. Both solve the same equations to residuals of 1e-8 or less, so the difference is the solvers' convergence only.

balances_on_every_stage.why: Proposal 0015: every stage's balances closed to 1e-8. Material: |residual| / F; energy: |residual| / (F x 10 kJ/mol); summation and equilibrium are mole fractions.

stability.why: one-liquid stages: no trial liquid on a grid has a tangent-plane distance below -1e-9

agreement_with_data.note: The three NRTL sets are fitted to vapour-liquid data; their liquid-liquid split is W1's work (joint fits, M2b) and not a test of the column.
